claim: [1] Citation review is distinct from answer plausibility; general principle corroborated by NIST and ALCE.
[3] SummEval separately evaluates consistency, coherence, fluency and relevance in English news summaries.
[4] QAFactEval metric results depend on learned QA components in its benchmark setting.
[5] ALCE measures citation support and relevance separately from answer correctness; exact method single-source.
[6] MT-Bench study reports useful preference agreement and position/verbosity bias in tested judges.
[7] NBME single-best-answer guidance recommends focused questions, one best key and plausible comparable options; educational-domain transfer remains proposal.
[8] Original prose study reports delayed retrieval-practice benefits; not an AI Study Buddy trial.
[9] Original MCQ feedback abstract reports later recall benefits and reduced distractor intrusions; full methods not inspected.
